correctness.rationale: The shift has return lengths p+1 where p is prime; 0<t<1/3 ensures a unique Gibbs parameter s>0 with mean return length 1/t. Kac and Abramov give h_mu<=t H(q); KL comparison with q_s proportional exp[-s(p+1)] gives h_mu/t<=log Z(s)+s/t with equality uniquely for the iid stationary renewal law and no zero fixed-point atom. Effective PNT plus Laplace integration yield Z(s)=s^-1[L^-1+gamma L^-2+(gamma^2+pi^2/6)L^-3+O(L^-4)], M(s)=s^-2[L^-1+(gamma-1)L^-2+(gamma^2+pi^2/6-2gamma)L^-3+O(L^-4)], L=log(1/s). Therefore s/t=1-L^-1-gamma L^-2+O(L^-3), Q=log(1/t)=L-L^-1-(gamma+1/2)L^-2+O(L^-3). Series inversion and substitution yield E(t)/t=Q-log Q+1+gamma/Q+(gamma^2/2+pi^2/6-1/2)/Q^2+O(Q^-3). Independently rederived the full displayed coefficient by symbolic series manipulation. The prime number theorem and rigorous tails, not finite prime sieves, support the unbounded prime-set asymptotic.

value.rationale: For a natural arithmetic S-gap shift, fixed rare-marker density entropy is a motivated invariant distinct from global topological entropy. The explicit log-log penalty and Euler/Gamma second and third corrections quantify the influence of prime density in a regime where the ordinary renewal variational identity alone does not supply the answer. Boundaries (t in (0,1/3), t->0, actual numbers of zero symbols prime) are precise.
